report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are vague and stakeholder-driven with no defined scope, technology stack, or team experience level specified, forcing an adaptive approach with iterative refinement.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Improve how projects are tracked internally
project_understanding.beneficiary: UNKNOWN — unclear which team or department will use this system
project_understanding.trigger: Current project tracking process is inadequate, but specific pain point not stated
success_definition: UNKNOWN — no metrics provided for what 'improved' means
supporting_quotes: We need to improve how we track projects.

assumption_log.what: This is a new internal tool build (TYPE_A) rather than an enhancement to an existing system or a data pipeline
assumption_log.why: Input mentions 'improve how we track' which suggests a new or replacement system, not a feature addition to existing software
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope definition requires understanding whether this is greenfield or brownfield work
assumption_log.consequence: If this is actually an enhancement to an existing project management tool, the team composition, integration points, and regression testing requirements change entirely, invalidating the phase structure
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows classification and phase decomposition to proceed. Risks: if the organization already has a project tracking system and this is a feature expansion, the plan will be fundamentally wrong.

assumption_log.what: The intended end users are internal project managers or team leads, not external customers
assumption_log.why: Input says 'improve how we track projects' — standard language for internal process improvement, not customer-facing product
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder identification requires understanding who benefits from the deliverable
assumption_log.consequence: If end users are different (e.g., executives, finance, external clients), the feature set, UI/UX requirements, and success metrics change significantly
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows persona definition and success criteria to be assumed. Risks: if wrong, UAT and adoption will fail because the tool was built for the wrong audience.

assumption_log.what: No technology stack is mandated; the team will choose the appropriate platform based on organizational standards
assumption_log.why: Input contains no mention of required technology, existing systems, or platform constraints
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource planning requires understanding available technology and team capability
assumption_log.consequence: If a specific technology is mandated by IT or compliance (e.g., 'must run on Salesforce', 'must be cloud-only'), the architecture, team skills, and timeline change
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows team to select best-fit technology. Risks: if a mandate exists and is discovered mid-project, rework is required.

assumption_log.what: No deadline is specified; planning assumes a standard 12-16 week delivery window for a TYPE_A internal tool with a 3-person core team
assumption_log.why: Input provides no date constraint; internal tools typically follow a predictable cadence unless otherwise stated
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline derived from scope and resource availability; absence of constraint allows standard estimation
assumption_log.consequence: If a hard deadline exists (e.g., 'must launch by Q2'), the phase allocations, team size, and scope must be re-negotiated immediately
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows realistic timeline estimation without compression. Risks: if a deadline exists and is not communicated, the plan will be invalidated on first stakeholder review.

assumption_log.what: No budget constraint is specified; planning assumes budget is available to hire or allocate necessary roles (PM, developers, QA, DevOps)
assumption_log.why: Input contains no mention of budget limits or cost constraints
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 7.2 — Cost estimation requires understanding budget availability; absence of constraint allows full-cost planning
assumption_log.consequence: If budget is constrained (e.g., 'max $50k'), team size, timeline, and scope must be reduced immediately
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows realistic staffing without artificial compression. Risks: if budget is limited and not disclosed, the plan will be rejected at approval.

assumption_log.what: Success is defined as 'adoption by end users' and 'reduction in time spent on manual project tracking' — measurable by post-launch survey and time-tracking data
assumption_log.why: Input says 'improve' but provides no metrics; standard success definition for internal tools is adoption and efficiency gain
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 — Quality metrics must be defined before execution; absence requires assumption of standard internal tool success criteria
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders define success differently (e.g., 'must integrate with Jira', 'must support 500 concurrent users'), the feature set and testing scope change
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows UAT and acceptance criteria to be defined. Risks: if stakeholder expectations differ, the tool will be rejected post-launch.

assumption_log.what: Stakeholder approval of scope, timeline, and budget is assumed to be pending — this plan is a proposal for stakeholder review, not a committed baseline
assumption_log.why: Input is a single sentence with no evidence of stakeholder sign-off or formal requirements document
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements and stakeholder approval before execution
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders reject the proposed scope, timeline, or team composition, the entire plan must be reworked
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning to proceed without stakeholder delay. Risks: if stakeholders have undisclosed expectations, the plan will be invalidated at review.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Product Manager and Backend Developer must be allocated full-time across all phases; Frontend Developer must be full-time Phases 2-4; QA Engineer must be full-time Phases 3-4. Any part-time allocation or shared resource will break the critical path.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: User personas and success metrics defined

tasks.name: Conduct stakeholder interviews to define project tracking pain points
tasks.definition_of_done: Interview notes from at least 3 stakeholders documenting current process, pain points, and desired outcomes

tasks.name: Map current project tracking workflow and identify bottlenecks
tasks.definition_of_done: Process flow diagram showing current state, identified bottlenecks, and time spent on each step

tasks.name: Define user personas, success metrics, and MVP scope
tasks.definition_of_done: Persona document with 2-3 user types, success metrics (adoption %, time saved), and MVP feature list approved by stakeholder

tasks.name: Design system architecture and technology stack recommendation
tasks.definition_of_done: Architecture document with technology stack, data model, and integration points reviewed by tech lead

tasks.name: Create wireframes for core project tracking workflows
tasks.definition_of_done: Wireframes for 5+ core screens showing project list, detail view, status updates, and reporting

tasks.name: Obtain stakeholder sign-off on requirements and MVP scope
tasks.definition_of_done: Signed requirements document and scope approval from primary stakeholder

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Data model and API endpoints implemented
Internal demo completed with stakeholder feedback

tasks.name: Set up development environment and CI/CD pipeline
tasks.definition_of_done: Development environment running locally, CI/CD pipeline configured and tested

tasks.name: Implement database schema and data access layer
tasks.definition_of_done: Database schema created, migrations tested, ORM/data access layer implemented and unit tested

tasks.name: Build project CRUD API endpoints
tasks.definition_of_done: Create, read, update, delete endpoints for projects implemented, documented, and tested with Postman/Swagger

tasks.name: Implement user authentication and role-based access control
tasks.definition_of_done: SSO or local authentication working, role-based access control enforced on all endpoints, tested with multiple user roles

tasks.name: Build frontend UI for project list and detail views
tasks.definition_of_done: Project list page and detail page rendering correctly, connected to backend API, responsive design tested on desktop and tablet

tasks.name: Implement project status update and notification features
tasks.definition_of_done: Status update form working, notifications sent to stakeholders, tested end-to-end

tasks.name: Conduct internal demo and gather stakeholder feedback
tasks.definition_of_done: Demo completed with stakeholders, feedback documented, prioritized backlog of changes created

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: Edge case handling implemented (bulk operations, error scenarios)
Performance testing at expected load completed

tasks.name: Implement email notifications for project updates
tasks.definition_of_done: Email notifications sent on project status change, tested with multiple recipients, unsubscribe option working

tasks.name: Build project reporting and export functionality
tasks.definition_of_done: Reports generated for project status, timeline, and resource allocation; CSV/PDF export working

tasks.name: Implement bulk project operations and import functionality
tasks.definition_of_done: Bulk update, delete, and CSV import working; error handling for malformed data; rollback on failure

tasks.name: Conduct security review and implement security hardening
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review completed, vulnerabilities identified and remediated, OWASP Top 10 checklist passed

tasks.name: Perform load testing and optimize performance
tasks.definition_of_done: Load test completed for 100 concurrent users, response times < 2s, database queries optimized

tasks.name: Execute comprehensive test plan and log defects
tasks.definition_of_done: Test plan executed, all test cases documented, defects logged in tracking system with severity and priority

tasks.name: Conduct user acceptance testing with stakeholders
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT completed with at least 2 end users, sign-off obtained, feedback incorporated

tasks.name: Perform accessibility audit and remediate issues
tasks.definition_of_done: Accessibility audit completed using WAVE/Axe, WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified, keyboard navigation tested

tasks.name: Create user documentation and training materials
tasks.definition_of_done: User guide, video tutorials, and FAQ documentation completed and reviewed by stakeholder

tasks.name: Create operational runbooks and monitoring setup
tasks.definition_of_done: Runbooks for common operations, monitoring alerts configured, on-call procedures documented

tasks.name: Deploy to production and execute smoke tests
tasks.definition_of_done: Application deployed to production, smoke tests passed, no critical errors in logs

tasks.name: Conduct go-live readiness review and stakeholder sign-off
tasks.definition_of_done: Go-live checklist completed, stakeholder sign-off obtained, post-launch support plan confirmed

tasks.name: Handoff to operations and activate post-launch support
tasks.definition_of_done: Operations team trained, support tickets configured, escalation procedures documented

risk_register.description: If scope is not formally defined and signed off by stakeholders before Phase 2 begins, then feature creep and scope changes will occur mid-project, causing timeline slippage and budget overrun
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests new features or changes requirements after development has started
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written scope approval from all stakeholders in Phase 1 before any development begins; establish change control process
risk_register.contingency: If scope changes are requested, evaluate impact on timeline and budget; prioritize changes and defer non-critical items to Phase 2

risk_register.description: If the team lacks experience with the selected technology stack, then development velocity will be lower than estimated, causing timeline slippage
risk_register.trigger: Development team reports unfamiliarity with selected framework or database technology
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct technology assessment in Phase 1; allocate time for team training before development begins; consider hiring contractor with expertise if needed
risk_register.contingency: If velocity is lower than expected, extend timeline or reduce scope; allocate additional resources for knowledge transfer

risk_register.description: If integration with existing project management systems (Jira, Asana, Monday.com) is required but not scoped, then additional development effort will be needed, causing timeline slippage
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests integration with external project management tool during Phase 2 or later
risk_register.mitigation: Clarify integration requirements in Phase 1; document all external system dependencies and API contracts before development begins
risk_register.contingency: If integration is required, evaluate effort and timeline impact; defer to Phase 2 if necessary

risk_register.description: If no deadline is communicated and stakeholders expect launch by a specific date, then the plan will be invalidated and timeline will need to be compressed
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder reveals expected launch date that conflicts with planned 14-week timeline
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm deadline and business drivers in Phase 1 kickoff meeting; document in requirements
risk_register.contingency: If deadline is earlier than planned, reduce scope or increase team size; evaluate budget impact

risk_register.description: If security or compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR) are not identified in Phase 1, then security review and remediation will be required late in the project, causing timeline slippage
risk_register.trigger: Compliance requirement discovered during Phase 3 or Phase 4 security review
risk_register.mitigation: Ask stakeholders explicitly about compliance requirements in Phase 1; document all regulatory constraints before design begins
risk_register.contingency: If compliance requirement is discovered late, allocate additional time for security review and remediation; defer non-critical features

risk_register.description: If the Product Manager is not allocated full-time to this project, then stakeholder alignment and decision-making will be delayed, causing timeline slippage
risk_register.trigger: PM is pulled to other projects or allocated part-time to this project
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm PM full-time allocation in writing before Phase 1 begins; establish escalation path for urgent decisions
risk_register.contingency: If PM is unavailable, assign a backup PM or delegate decision-making authority to a named stakeholder

risk_register.description: If this is the team's first project of this type (building an internal project tracking tool), then execution risk is elevated due to unfamiliarity with requirements and best practices
risk_register.trigger: Team reports lack of experience with similar projects or domain knowledge
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate time for team training and knowledge transfer in Phase 1; consider hiring domain expert or contractor
risk_register.contingency: If execution issues arise, extend timeline or allocate additional resources for problem-solving

risk_register.description: If email notification service or external API dependencies are not tested in sandbox before Phase 2, then integration failures will occur during development, causing rework
risk_register.trigger: Email service or external API is unavailable or has unexpected behavior during development
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm sandbox access and API documentation for all external services in Phase 1; test integration points early in Phase 2
risk_register.contingency: If integration fails, implement fallback or alternative service; allocate time for troubleshooting

risk_register.description: If QA Engineer is not allocated at minimum 25% of total development effort, then test coverage will be insufficient and critical bugs will reach production
risk_register.trigger: QA effort falls below 25% of development hours due to resource constraints
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate QA Engineer at 25% minimum of total development hours; establish test plan in Phase 1
risk_register.contingency: If QA is under-allocated, extend Phase 4 timeline or reduce scope to match available QA capacity

risk_register.description: If end-user adoption is not planned and communicated, then the tool will be built but not used, resulting in project failure despite technical success
risk_register.trigger: Post-launch, end users do not adopt the tool due to lack of training or communication
risk_register.mitigation: Develop adoption plan in Phase 1; conduct training sessions before launch; communicate benefits to end users
risk_register.contingency: If adoption is low post-launch, conduct user feedback sessions and iterate on features; provide additional training
